item.title: China's solar capacity set to surpass coal for first time in 2026
item.description: The United States and China are both on track to add record amounts of clean energy capacity in 2026, driven by falling technology costs and surging electricity demand, even as the two countries face divergent policy headwinds that threaten to slow the pace of the transition.

item.title: Trump orders extended Iran blockade after rejecting Tehran's proposal
item.description:
President Trump has effectively rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, instead directing aides to prepare for a prolonged naval blockade of Iranian ports, according to The Wall Street Journal. The decision, reached during a Monday Situation Room meeting with his national security team, marks an escalation in the two-month-old conflict that has disrupted roughly one-fifth of the world's oil supply.

Iran's proposal, first reported by Axios and The Associated Press on Sunday, offered to jointly reopen the strait and extend the current ceasefire while postponing discussions on Tehran's nuclear program to a later date. Sources told CBS News that the deal was conditional on the U.S. lifting its blockade of Iranian ports.

item.title: Putin proposes Victory Day truce in Ukraine during call with Trump
item.description:
President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin spoke by phone on Wednesday in a wide-ranging conversation that touched on the war in Iran, peace efforts in Ukraine, and the recent shooting at the White House Correspondents' Dinner, according to the Kremlin.

The call, which lasted roughly 90 minutes, was confirmed by Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov, who told reporters that Putin proposed ideas for resolving the Iran conflict and expressed readiness to declare a truce in Ukraine for Russia's Victory Day celebrations on May 9. It was the first known direct conversation between the two leaders since a similar call in March.

item.title: Perovskite device sets records as both solar cell and LED
item.description: A single perovskite device has achieved world-record performance in both solar energy conversion and light emission, a feat that had previously been accomplished only by costly single-crystal gallium arsenide. The study, published in Joule, describes a diode that converts sunlight to electricity at 26.7% efficiency and emits light with an external quantum efficiency of roughly 31%, demonstrating that the long-standing divide between photovoltaic and LED device design is an engineering problem rather than a physical limitation.

item.title: London stabbing of 2 Jewish men declared terrorist attack
item.description:
Two Jewish men were stabbed on the streets of north London on Wednesday morning in what police have formally declared a terrorist incident, marking the latest in a series of antisemitic attacks to strike the capital's Jewish community.

The attack occurred at approximately 11:16 a.m. on Highfield Avenue in Barnet, near Golders Green, a neighborhood home to one of London's largest Jewish populations. The victims, aged 76 and 34, suffered knife wounds and were taken to hospital, where they are reported to be in stable condition.

item.title: Trump calls UAE's exit from OPEC 'great' for fuel prices
item.description:
President Donald Trump on Wednesday welcomed the United Arab Emirates' decision to withdraw from OPEC, calling the move "great" and framing it as a win for American consumers grappling with surging fuel costs amid the ongoing war with Iran.

"I think it's great," Trump told reporters. "Ultimately, it's a good thing for getting the price of gas down, getting oil down, getting everything down." Trump, who has previously accused OPEC of "ripping off the rest of the world," also praised UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed, calling him "a great leader" and adding, "He probably maybe wants to go his own way. That's a good thing."

item.title: Israel sets two-week deadline for Lebanon deal, warns of escalation
item.description: Israel has given US-mediated negotiations with Lebanon a two-week window to produce a permanent agreement, warning it will resume intensive military operations against Hezbollah if diplomacy fails by mid-May, according to multiple reports citing Israeli officials.

item.title: Trump says US reviewing troop reduction in Germany
item.description:
President Donald Trump announced on Wednesday that his administration is reviewing a possible reduction of American military forces stationed in Germany, escalating pressure on NATO allies who have refused to support the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. "The United States is studying and reviewing the possible reduction of Troops in Germany, with a determination to be made over the next short period of time," Trump wrote on Truth Social.

The move comes amid a growing transatlantic rift. The U.S. currently has just over 68,000 active-duty military personnel permanently assigned to bases across Europe, with more than half — about 36,400 — stationed in Germany, according to data from the U.S. Defense Manpower Data Center cited by Reuters.

item.title: Zelenskyy demands details on Victory Day ceasefire after Trump-Putin call
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin spoke by phone on Wednesday, April 29, in a conversation lasting more than 90 minutes that ended with Putin proposing a temporary ceasefire in Ukraine to mark Russia's May 9 Victory Day holiday — and competing claims over who originated the idea.

item.title: Iran's Khamenei vows to defend nuclear capabilities after Trump-Putin call
item.description:
President Donald Trump on Wednesday disclosed that Russian President Vladimir Putin had offered to help resolve the standoff over Iran's enriched uranium stockpile during a 90-minute phone call, but said he told Putin he would prefer the Kremlin prioritize ending its war in Ukraine.

"He told me he'd like to be involved with the enrichment — if he can help us get it," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office on April 29. "I said, 'I'd much rather have you be involved with ending the war with Ukraine.' To me, that would be more important."

item.title: Trump escalates feud with Merz, threatens troop cuts in Germany
item.description: President Donald Trump escalated a public dispute with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Thursday, telling the German leader to focus on ending the Russia-Ukraine war and fixing his "broken Country" rather than "interfering" with American efforts against Iran. The broadside came one day after Trump announced the U.S. was "studying and reviewing the possible reduction of Troops in Germany," raising the prospect of a drawdown from one of America's most strategically vital overseas military footprints.

item.title: China launches combat patrols near Scarborough Shoal amid US-Philippines drills
item.description: China's military announced on Thursday that its naval and air forces carried out combat readiness patrols near the disputed Scarborough Shoal in the South China Sea, a move that coincided with ongoing multinational military exercises led by the Philippines and the United States.

item.title: UAE bans citizens from traveling to Iran, Lebanon, and Iraq
item.description: The United Arab Emirates Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Thursday announced a travel ban prohibiting Emirati nationals from traveling to Iran, Lebanon, and Iraq, citing "current regional developments" as the two-month-old conflict between the United States and Iran continues to reshape the Middle East.

item.title: Israel rushed Iron Beam laser system to UAE to counter Iran attacks
item.description: Israel secretly deployed its newly operational Iron Beam laser air defense system to the United Arab Emirates to help counter Iran's sustained missile and drone bombardment, the Financial Times reported Thursday, in the latest revelation of deepening military cooperation between the two Abraham Accords partners.

item.title: Iran accelerates weapons recovery as ceasefire talks stall, NBC News reports
item.description: Iran is exploiting its ceasefire with the United States to unearth missiles, drones, and other munitions that were either hidden underground before the war or buried beneath rubble from American and Israeli airstrikes, according to an NBC News report citing a U.S. official and two other sources familiar with the matter.

item.title: Trump to raise tariffs on EU cars and trucks to 25%
item.description: President Donald Trump announced Friday that he will increase tariffs on cars and trucks imported from the European Union to 25%, accusing the bloc of failing to comply with the trade deal struck last year at Turnberry, Scotland. The move threatens to upend transatlantic trade relations at a moment when the EU is already navigating tensions on multiple fronts.

item.title: Trump says he's 'not satisfied' with Iran's latest proposal
item.description: President Donald Trump on Friday cast doubt on the prospect of reaching a deal with Iran, telling reporters at the White House that he was "not happy" with Tehran's latest negotiating proposal and warning he would "blast the hell out of them" if diplomacy fails.

item.title: US to shut Gaza ceasefire center as Trump plan stalls
item.description: The Trump administration is set to shut down the Civil-Military Coordination Centre (CMCC), the U.S. military-run facility in southern Israel that served as the centerpiece of Washington's effort to oversee the Israel-Hamas ceasefire and coordinate humanitarian aid to Gaza, according to an exclusive report by Reuters citing seven diplomats familiar with the centre's operations.

item.title: Iran demands six Arab states pay reparations over war
item.description: Iran's ambassador to the United Nations has formally demanded that six Arab states be held legally accountable for their role in facilitating the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, calling their actions acts of aggression under international law.

item.title: US warns EU allies of arms delivery delays as Iran war drains stockpiles
item.description:
The United States has warned European allies including the United Kingdom, Poland, Lithuania, and Estonia to expect prolonged delays in the delivery of American weapons systems, as the ongoing war with Iran rapidly depletes U.S. munitions stockpiles, the Financial Times reported on Friday.

The warning, delivered through bilateral channels, marks an expansion of earlier alerts that had been limited to Baltic and Scandinavian nations. It underscores how deeply the two-month-old conflict is straining America's defense industrial base and unsettling NATO allies already on edge over Russia.
